checks.evidence: Action: Observed startup motion, selected all rendered bodies, sought 0, 12, 24 and 48 seconds, and compared ordinary screenshots and native canvas picks with independently projected orbital positions. Expected: One Sun and exactly three differently sized/colored planets on fixed-phase circular 12/24/48-second orbits. Observed: One yellow Sun and small cyan Mercury, medium orange Venus and larger blue Earth. Mercury returned to its initial rendered location at 12, Venus at 24, and Earth at 48; intermediate bodies occupied different expected locations. Native picks at these expected locations selected the corresponding actual meshes. Phases were 12/126/248 degrees and measured live progression agreed with the period ratios.

Action: Opened the artifact and reloaded through an iframe load-event barrier, including with saved snapshots present. Expected: Time 0, speed 1x, running playback, no selection and overview, followed by motion. Observed: The immediate reload readout was 0.0/1x/LIVE, empty selection and FULL SYSTEM; saved snapshots did not restore live state. Subsequent sole-visible-scene sampling advanced 5.5 to 8.6 in 3.202 wall seconds, with moving planets. Initial later-loaded 5-second readouts were not misclassified as a reset defect.

Action: Paused, observed the scene over 3.203 wall seconds, sought 30, changed speed while paused, and resumed. Expected: Frozen time and all orbital locations, then continuous motion from the held state. Observed: Time stayed exactly 17.0 during the pause sample with unchanged orbital arrangement; at 30 all angles remained 192/216/113 degrees while paused. Resume from 30 at 2x progressed 30.4 to 36.8 over 3.202 seconds without a reset or visible position jump. Paused selection and camera operations also remained usable.

Action: Used native drag and wheel zoom in overview and tracking, both playing and paused, inspecting before/after rendered scenes.
